Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about Acme's summarization use case for your 100k+ token product manuals. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

What we heard:
- Primary need: faithful summaries across very long documents (30k-100k tokens) with tight truncation behavior and minimal information loss.
- Success metrics: ROUGE/ROUGE-L + human QA focused on missing facts and hallucinations.
- Constraints: some PII redaction required, and offline on-prem deployment is a future ask but initial eval will be on hosted Redwood sandbox.

Redwood recommended starting points:
- Model candidates to evaluate: Redwood-Longformer-13B-64k (best latency/cost tradeoff for long context), Llama2-70B-32k (quantized) for baseline, and a larger 70B-64k variant if you want maximal fidelity.
- Eval plan: run chunked + sliding-window summarization, end-to-end long-context summarization, and strict truncation tests (see attached evaluation_template.xlsx).
- Prompt sets: we'll share an initial prompt set focused on extractive anchors + abstractive synthesis (attached as acme_prompt_set_v1.json in follow-up).

Attachments:
- evaluation_template.xlsx (attached) — lightweight schema for logging ROUGE/human QA and truncation edge cases.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please share a representative sample (1–3 documents) — you mentioned a sanitized manual and a support ticket archive; if you can send one sample that shows the longest expected context, that will help.
2) We run a first-pass long-context eval (3 business days) and share results + prompt set tweaks.
3) Technical deep-dive with our SRE/Applied ML team to discuss KV cache behavior, tokenization tradeoffs, and deployment options.

If that works I'll schedule the deep-dive and loop in Neha and Rishi from our side.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi all,

We can take the quick pass — plan below: 

Planned tests (3 business day quick pass):
1) Inference runs (single-pass 64k) on Redwood-Longformer-13B-64k and Llama2-70B-32k-quant to collect latency and token-cost metrics.
2) End-preservation test: inject 25 labeled anchors in the last 1k tokens, verify recall in generated summary (binary pass/fail + examples).
3) Sliding-window vs single-pass comparison on the 78k doc to measure information loss and coherence.
4) Manual QA sample (10 items) to quantify hallucination/missing-fact rate.

Preliminary notes / risk flags:
- We saw in prior customers that some 32k models (even when chunked) can miss late-document facts unless prompts explicitly instruct to include end anchors — we'll test prompt sensitivity.
- For very long docs (>64k) we recommend a chunk+recap pipeline (chunk summarize + hierarchical synthesis) rather than single huge context, but Redwood-Longformer-13B-64k should preserve last 1k tokens consistently in our tests.
- KV-cache retention: if we do streaming generation with offloaded KV, need to validate our runtime paging behavior. We'll run that as part of the deep-dive if they go deeper.

Artifacts we'll produce: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (initial prompts + anchor tests), acme_eval_plan.md (detailed test plan), and a short results spreadsheet.

Estimate: quick pass in 3 business days; full run with 50 docs and human QA ~7–10 business days. Cost estimate for quick pass: ~$1.2k (compute + human QA sampling) — rough ballpark.

I'll start the runs tonight and post preliminary results to the shared Drive folder.
